standard-dialogue.npc: I am a mighty and powerful genie. Why do you come here? Speak now or I'll have to think of something exceedingly nasty to do to you.

options.text: You're a genie, grant me a wish.

steps.player: You're a genie, grant me a wish.

steps.npc: Not all genies are goody two shoes who go round granting wishes. It's something that my pathetic brother does to make people like him, but that's not my style.
I like to think of myself more as an evil and scary sort of genie, who people talk about in hushed and fearful tones.

options.text: Well you seem quite scary.

steps.npc: Why thank you, I put a lot of effort into my terrifyingness.
Wait! Did you say quite scary? I'll have you know I am VERY scary!

steps.player: Erm yes that's what I meant.

options.text: Why are you sitting here in the dark.
Well I must be off now.

steps.player: Well I must be off now.

steps.npc: Yes, run. Ruuuun in fear of.. The crevice genie of Nardah! Muhahaha!

options.text: Why are you sitting here in the dark?

steps.player: Why are you sitting here in the dark?

steps.npc: Two reasons really. Firstly, I can see in the dark, so light or dark makes little difference to me.
Lastly, I gather it's normal for powerful terrifying creatures to lurk around in dark caves, so I found this one to lurk in myself, nice isn't it?

options.text: Very pleasant, the snakes are a nice touch.

steps.player: Very pleasant, the snakes are a nice touch.

steps.npc: Why do I get the sense that I'm not being taken seriously here? Please try to remember I am very dangerous and not to be trifled with.

options.text: You're a genie, grant me a wish.
Well I must be off now.
I'm just looking around.

steps.npc: I don't know about that. I can't have just anybody traipsing in here. I have a reputation to keep you see.
Actually I'll tell you what, you can hang around here for a bit, but be sure to spread the word about what a terrifying experience you had when you ran into... The crevice genie of Nardah!

steps.player: ...Ok I think I can manage that.

attempting-to-take-the-lamp-on-his-table.npc: Hey get your hands off my house.

attempting-to-cast-any-spell-while-in-th.npc: Hey, no casting spells on my house!

during-spirits-of-the-elid.npc: I am a mighty and powerful genie. Why do you come here? Speak now or I'll have to think of something exceedingly nasty to do to you.

options.text: I'm after a statue that was thrown down here.

steps.player: I'm after a statue that was thrown down here.

steps.npc: Ahh yes someone did drop a statue on my head recently. Very nice workmanship, looks quite old and valuable too. I'm surprised someone threw it away!
I have accepted it as a gift as they clearly respect my terrible powers. They seek to keep me at bay by giving me valuables.

options.text: Maybe I can make a deal for it?

steps.player: Maybe I can make a deal for the statuette?

steps.npc: Hmm a deal eh? I think we can come to some sort of arrangement. I'll give you the valuable statuette in return for, let me think ....
How about I give you the statue in exchange for the sole of the mayor of Nardah?

options.text: Isn't that a little harsh?

steps.npc: I wouldn't have said so. It seems a perfectly reasonable thing to request to me. I can think of many things a lot worse I could have asked for.

options.text: How am I meant to remove someone's soul?

steps.player: How am I meant to remove someone's soul?

steps.npc: Oh that's easy. In my experience soles are very easy to remove with just a knife.

options.text: Ok I agree to the deal.

steps.player: Ok I agree to the deal.

options.text: No way am I agreeing to that.

steps.player: No way am I agreeing to that.

steps.npc: Ah well it's your loss. No sole, then no statuette.

options.text: I'm not sure they know you're down here.

steps.player: I'm not sure they know you're down here.

steps.npc: Silence cur! They fear and respect me and that's an end to it.

steps.player: Maybe I can make a deal for the statuette?

steps.npc: Hmm a deal eh? I think we can come to some sort of arrangement. I'll give you the valuable statuette in return for, let me think ....
How about I give you the statue in exchange for the sole of the mayor of Nardah?

options.text: Isn't that a little harsh?
How am I meant to remove someone's soul?
Ok I agree to the deal.
No way am I agreeing to that.
You're a genie, grant me a wish.
Why are you sitting here in the dark?
I'm just looking around.

during-spirits-of-the-elid-talking-to-hi.npc: Do you have the sole of Awusah, so that we can make our trade?

options.text: How am I meant to remove someone's soul?
I'm still working on it.

steps.npc: Well no rush, I quite like the statuette too.

options.text: No, it's not an easy thing to get.

steps.player: No, it's not an easy thing to get.

steps.npc: Haha, even a pathetic human should be able to manage to get another human's sole.

during-spirits-of-the-elid-talking-to-hi.npc: Do you have the sole of Awusah, so that we can make our trade?
Ah excellent, here's the statuette then.

during-spirits-of-the-elid-talking-to-hi.text: You trade the sole for the statuette.

during-spirits-of-the-elid-talking-to-hi.player: So um, why do you need part of Awusah's footwear anyway? I hope you're not going to do some nasty magic on his feet or something.

during-spirits-of-the-elid-talking-to-hi.npc: I hadn't thought of that. I just read that a lot of the most powerful beings are collecting soles these days. I haven't really got many yet though. You provided me with an opportunity to expand my collection.
Well fortunately for you, I am a mighty and powerful genie and managed to reacquire it. I will give it to you for another sole.

during-spirits-of-the-elid-talking-to-hi.player: I will go and get one then.

during-spirits-of-the-elid-talking-to-hi.npc: Great! Another one for my collection.
Well fortunately for you, I am a mighty and powerful genie and managed to reacquire it. I will give it to you for another sole.
Ah excellent here's the statuette then.
It's good doing business with you again.
